`react-virtualized` is a set of React components for efficiently rendering large lists and tabular data. > [!TIP] > If you're considering adding `react-virtualized` to a project, take a look at [`react-window`](https://react-window.vercel.app/) as a possible lighter-weight alternative. ## Support If you like this project there are several ways to support it: - [Become a GitHub sponsor](https://github.com/sponsors/bvaughn/) - [Become an Open Collective sponsor](https://opencollective.com/react-virtualized#sponsor) - or [buy me a coffee](http://givebrian.coffee/) The following wonderful companies and individuals have sponsored react-virtualized: ## Installation Begin by installing the library from NPM: ```sh npm install react-virtualized ``` Most of react-virtualized's styles are functional (e.g. position, size) and are applied directly to DOM elements. The `Table` component also ships with a few optional presentational styles; to use them, import the CSS file once (e.g. while bootstrapping your application): ```js import "react-virtualized/styles.css"; ``` The package is marked as side-effect free (other than its CSS), so bundlers will tree-shake any components you don't use. ## TypeScript types TypeScript definitions are included within the published `dist` folder. Types are exported for each component's props (e.g. `ListProps`, `GridProps`, `TableProps`) along with the parameters passed to renderers (e.g. `RowRendererParams`, `CellRendererParams`, `TableCellProps`). ## Pure components By default all react-virtualized components are wrapped in [`memo`](https://react.dev/reference/react/memo) to avoid re-rendering unless props or state has changed. This occasionally confuses users when a collection's data changes (eg `['a','b','c']` => `['d','e','f']`) but props do not (eg `array.length`). The solution to this is to let react-virtualized know that something external has changed. This can be done a couple of different ways. ### Pass-thru props This shallow comparison will detect changes to any props, even ones a component doesn't use. This means you can also pass through additional properties that affect cell rendering to ensure changes are detected. For example, if you're using `List` to render a list of items that may be re-sorted after initial render- react-virtualized would not normally detect the sort operation because none of the properties it deals with change. However you can pass through the additional sort property to trigger a re-render. For example: ```js ``` ### Public methods `Grid` components can be forcefully re-rendered by calling [`forceUpdate`](https://react-virtualized-docs.vercel.app/grid/methods#forceUpdate) on their ref. For `Table` and `List`, you'll need to call [`forceUpdateGrid`](https://react-virtualized-docs.vercel.app/table/methods#forceUpdateGrid) to ensure that the inner `Grid` is also updated. For `MultiGrid`, you'll need to call [`forceUpdateGrids`](https://react-virtualized-docs.vercel.app/grid/multi-grid-methods#forceUpdateGrids) to ensure that the inner `Grid`s are updated. ## Documentation Documentation and live examples for every component are available at [react-virtualized-docs.vercel.app](https://react-virtualized-docs.vercel.app/), along with how-to guides for things like [sizing components](https://react-virtualized-docs.vercel.app/guides/sizing-components), [infinite loading](https://react-virtualized-docs.vercel.app/guides/infinite-loading-list) and [server rendering](https://react-virtualized-docs.vercel.app/guides/server-rendering). > [!NOTE] > `AutoSizer` is no longer part of react-virtualized (as of version 10); it is available as the separate [`react-virtualized-auto-sizer`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/react-virtualized-auto-sizer) package. ## Components ### ArrowKeyStepper This HOC decorates a virtualized component and responds to arrow-key events by scrolling one row or column at a time. This provides a snap-to behavior rather than the default browser scrolling behavior. Note that unlike the other HOCs in react-virtualized, `ArrowKeyStepper` adds a `
` element around its children in order to attach a key-down event handler. The appearance of this wrapper element can be customized using the `className` property. #### Required props
Name Description
children

Function responsible for rendering children. It is passed onSectionRendered and registerChild parameters, which should be attached to the decorated virtualized component (e.g. <Grid onSectionRendered={onSectionRendered} ref={registerChild} />), and the scrollToColumn and scrollToRow indices of the active cell (e.g. to highlight it). The active cell is scrolled into view through the registered component's scrollToCell method.
columnCount

Number of columns in grid; for Table and List this property should always be 1.
rowCount

Number of rows in grid.
#### Optional props
Name Description
className

CSS class name to attach to the wrapper <div>.
disabled

Disables all scrolling using arrow-keys.
isControlled

This component is "controlled"; it will not update scrollToColumn or scrollToRow itself. This property should be used with onScrollToChange.
mode

Controls behavior of stepper when arrow key direction changes. "cells" means that the index will only increment or decrement by 1; "edges" means that the opposite side of the grid will be incremented.
onScrollToChange

Called when arrow key navigation should update the current scroll-to values.
scrollToColumn

Default/initial scrollToColumn value. When isControlled is true, this is the current scrollToColumn value.
scrollToRow

Default/initial scrollToRow value. When isControlled is true, this is the current scrollToRow value.
### CellMeasurer Wraps a cell and measures its rendered content. Measurements are stored in a per-cell cache. Cached-content is not be re-measured. The child must be a DOM element (e.g. `
`) or a component that passes its `ref` along to one; otherwise use a function child and pass `registerChild` as the `ref` of the element to be measured. #### Required props
Name Description
cache

Cache to be shared between CellMeasurer and its parent Grid. Typically an instance of CellMeasurerCache.
children

Either a React element as a child (eg <div />) or a function (eg. ({ measure, registerChild }) => <div ref={registerChild} />).

CellMeasurer attaches a ref to the child element to find the DOM element to measure (the child's own ref, if any, still receives the element). So the child must be a DOM element (e.g. <div>) or a component that passes its ref along to one: in React 19, a function component can pass its ref prop to a DOM element; in React 18, function components must use forwardRef for this.

The function receives a measure callback (to re-measure the cell, e.g. after an image has loaded) and a registerChild callback (to specify the DOM element to be measured; can be used as a ref). Use registerChild if the child doesn't pass its ref along to a DOM element, or to measure an element nested within the child.

Children that can't be measured (e.g. text, an array or a fragment, without registerChild) are rendered as-is, and a warning is logged in development mode.
parent

Reference to the parent Grid (or List, Table, MultiGrid, Masonry); this value is passed by Grid to the cellRenderer and should be passed along as-is.
#### Optional props
Name Description
columnIndex

Index of column being measured (within the parent Grid) or 0 (if used within a List or Table).
index

Index of row being measured; alias of rowIndex (as passed to a List row renderer). Only used if rowIndex is not specified.
rowIndex

Index of row being measured (within the parent Grid). Defaults to index (or 0 if neither is specified).
### Column Describes the header and cell contents of a table column. This component does not render anything itself; `Table` reads the props of its children to render headers and cells (applying `defaultColumnProps` to each child's props). Components that render a `Column` (e.g. `const MyColumn = (props) => `) can be used as `Table` children too; their props are read the same way (the wrapper component itself is never rendered). #### Required props
Name Description
dataKey

Uniquely identifies the row-data attribute corresponding to this cell (eg this might be "name" in an array of user objects).
width

Flex basis (width) for this column; This value can grow or shrink based on flexGrow and flexShrink properties.
#### Optional props
Name Description
aria-label

Optional aria-label value to set on the column header.
cellDataGetter

Callback responsible for returning a cell's data, given its dataKey: ({ columnData: any, dataKey: string, rowData: any }): any.

The default cellDataGetter expects to operate on either a vanilla Object or a Map-like object with a get method. You should override it if your data is calculated or requires any custom processing. Defaults to defaultTableCellDataGetter.
cellRenderer

Callback responsible for rendering a cell's contents: ({ cellData: any, columnData: any, columnIndex: number, dataKey: string, isScrolling: boolean, parent: TableImperativeAPI, rowData: any, rowIndex: number }): ReactNode.

The default cellRenderer (defaultTableCellRenderer) displays an attribute as a simple string. You should override it if your data is some other type of object or requires custom formatting.
className

Optional CSS class to apply to the rendered cell container.
columnData

Additional data passed to this column's cellDataGetter, cellRenderer, and headerRenderer. Use this object to relay action-creators or relational data.
defaultSortDirection

Default sort order when clicked for the first time.
disableSort

If sort is enabled for the table at large, disable it for this column.
flexGrow

Flex grow style.
flexShrink

Flex shrink style.
headerClassName

Optional CSS class to apply to this column's header.
headerRenderer

Optional callback responsible for rendering a column's header contents: ({ columnData: any, dataKey: string, disableSort: boolean, label: ReactNode, sortBy: string, sortDirection: SortDirection }): ReactNode.

The default headerRenderer (defaultTableHeaderRenderer) displays the column label along with a sort indicator if the column is sort-enabled and active.
headerStyle

Optional inline style to apply to this column's header.
id

Optional id to set on the column header; used for the cells' aria-describedby.
label

Header label for this column.
maxWidth

Maximum width of column; this property will only be used if flexGrow is greater than 0.
minWidth

Minimum width of column.
style

Optional inline style to apply to the rendered cell container.
### ColumnSizer High-order component that auto-calculates column-widths for `Grid` cells. #### Required props
Name Description
children

Function responsible for rendering a virtualized Grid. It is passed { adjustedWidth, columnWidth, getColumnWidth, registerChild }.

The columnWidth value should be passed to the Grid's columnWidth property, and registerChild should be passed to the Grid's ref property. The adjustedWidth value is optional; it reflects the lesser of the overall width or the width of all columns.
columnCount

Number of columns in the Grid or Table child.
width

Width of the Grid or Table child.
#### Optional props
Name Description
columnMaxWidth

Optional maximum allowed column width.
columnMinWidth

Optional minimum allowed column width.
### Grid Renders tabular data with virtualization along the vertical and horizontal axes. Row heights and column widths must be known ahead of time and specified as properties. Scrolling is done through the imperative handle (`ref`): see `scrollToCell` and `scrollToPosition`. #### Required props
Name Description
cellRenderer

Responsible for rendering a cell given an row and column index. It receives columnIndex, isScrolling, isVisible, key, parent, rowIndex, and style parameters.

The style parameter specifies how the cell is to be sized and positioned and must be passed through to the rendered cell element. The key parameter must also be applied to the rendered element.
columnCount

Number of columns in grid.
columnWidth

Either a fixed column width (number) or a function that returns the width of a column given its index: ({ index: number }): number. If function is used, specify estimatedColumnSize for more consistent scrolling behavior.
rowCount

Number of rows in grid.
rowHeight

Either a fixed row height (number) or a function that returns the height of a row given its index: ({ index: number }): number. If function is used, specify estimatedRowSize for more consistent scrolling behavior.
width

Width of Grid; this property determines the number of visible (vs virtualized) columns.
#### Optional props
Name Description
aria-label

ARIA label for the grid element.
aria-readonly

ARIA readonly attribute for the grid element.
autoContainerWidth

Set the width of the inner scrollable container to 'auto'. This is useful for single-column Grids to ensure that the column doesn't extend below a vertical scrollbar.
cellRangeRenderer

Responsible for rendering a group of cells given their index ranges.

This is an advanced property. It is useful for situations where the Grid requires additional, overlayed UI (such as a Gantt chart or a calendar application). The easiest way to override it is to decorate defaultCellRangeRenderer.

Defaults to defaultCellRangeRenderer.
className

Optional custom CSS class name to attach to root Grid element.
containerProps

Additional props (eg onWheel) to spread onto the outer Grid element.
containerRole

ARIA role for the inner cell-container.
containerStyle

Optional custom inline style to attach to inner cell-container element.
deferredMeasurementCache

If CellMeasurer is used to measure this Grid's children, this should be a pointer to its CellMeasurerCache. A shared CellMeasurerCache reference enables Grid and CellMeasurer to share measurement data.
elementRef

Reference to the outer (scrolling) DOM element.
estimatedColumnSize

Used to estimate the total width of a Grid before all of its columns have actually been measured. The estimated total width is adjusted as columns are rendered.
estimatedRowSize

Used to estimate the total height of a Grid before all of its rows have actually been measured. The estimated total height is adjusted as rows are rendered.
getScrollbarSize

Returns the size of the browser's scrollbar. Exposed for testing purposes only.

Defaults to dom-helpers' scrollbarSize (which returns undefined during server rendering).
height

Height of Grid; this property determines the number of visible (vs virtualized) rows. Required, unless a scrollElement is specified.

With a scrollElement, the height of the scroll element's viewport is used instead; this prop is then only used until the scroll element has been measured (e.g. during server rendering).
id

Optional custom id to attach to root Grid element.
initialScrollLeft

Horizontal scroll offset to initially render (and scroll to) the Grid at. Only the initial value is used: changing this prop later has no effect (use scrollToPosition to scroll). This also works with server rendering: the cells at this offset are rendered on the server, and they stay in place when the page is hydrated.
initialScrollTop

Vertical scroll offset to initially render (and scroll to) the Grid at. Only the initial value is used: changing this prop later has no effect (use scrollToPosition to scroll). This also works with server rendering: the cells at this offset are rendered on the server, and they stay in place when the page is hydrated. Ignored if a scrollElement is specified (which then determines the vertical offset).
isScrollingOptOut

Prevents re-rendering of visible cells on scroll end. (Opts out of the isScrolling param passed to cellRangeRenderer, to avoid the extra render when scroll stops.) Visible cells are still re-rendered when the Grid's props change or forceUpdate() is called.
noContentRenderer

Optional renderer to be rendered inside the grid when either rowCount or columnCount is empty. Renders nothing by default.
onScroll

Callback invoked whenever the scroll offset changes within the inner scrollable region: ({ clientHeight: number, clientWidth: number, scrollHeight: number, scrollLeft: number, scrollTop: number, scrollWidth: number }): void. This callback can be used to sync scrolling between lists, tables, or grids.
onScrollbarPresenceChange

Called whenever a horizontal or vertical scrollbar is added or removed: ({ horizontal: boolean, size: number, vertical: boolean }): void. This prop is not intended for end-user use; it is used by MultiGrid to support fixed-row/fixed-column scroll syncing.
onSectionRendered

Callback invoked with information about the section of the Grid that was just rendered. This callback is only invoked when visible rows have changed: ({ columnOverscanStartIndex: number, columnOverscanStopIndex: number, columnStartIndex: number, columnStopIndex: number, rowOverscanStartIndex: number, rowOverscanStopIndex: number, rowStartIndex: number, rowStopIndex: number }): void.
overscanColumnCount

Number of columns to render before/after the visible slice of the grid. This can help reduce flickering during scrolling on certain browsers/devices.

Note that this property has performance implications: the higher the value, the more work needs to be done in reaction to each scroll event. Aim to use the lowest value possible that still generally avoids any empty space from appearing during normal scrolling.
overscanIndicesGetter

Responsible for calculating the number of cells to overscan before and after a specified range. By default, cells are overscanned in the direction the user is scrolling. This function receives direction, cellCount, scrollDirection, overscanCellsCount, startIndex, and stopIndex parameters and returns an { overscanStartIndex, overscanStopIndex } object.

Defaults to defaultOverscanIndicesGetter.
overscanRowCount

Number of rows to render above/below the visible slice of the grid. This can help reduce flickering during scrolling on certain browsers/devices.

Note that this property has performance implications: the higher the value, the more work needs to be done in reaction to each scroll event. The default value (10) is a good starting point; lower it if possible.
role

Optional override of ARIA role default.
scrollElement

Element that scrolls the Grid (instead of the Grid scrolling itself): "window", or a scrollable DOM element (e.g. a container that the Grid is rendered within, along with other content).

The Grid then renders at its full height (it may still scroll horizontally itself), renders only the rows visible within the scroll element's viewport, and its scroll methods scroll the scroll element. Its position within the scroll element is measured when the scroll element scrolls or is resized, and when the Grid re-renders (e.g. call forceUpdate() if content above the Grid changes size without the Grid re-rendering). Pass null while the scroll element isn't available yet (e.g. before a ref to it has been attached); the Grid then renders the rows at its top.
scrollingResetTimeInterval

Wait this amount of time (in milliseconds) after the last scroll event before resetting Grid pointer-events.
style

Optional custom inline style to attach to root Grid element.
tabIndex

Optional override of tab index default.
### InfiniteLoader Higher-order component that manages lazy-loading for "infinite" data. This component decorates a virtual component and just-in-time prefetches rows as a user scrolls. It is intended as a convenience component; fork it if you'd like finer-grained control over data-loading. #### Required props
Name Description
children

Function responsible for rendering a virtualized component. It is passed onRowsRendered and registerChild parameters. The onRowsRendered function should be passed through to the child's onRowsRendered property. The registerChild callback should be set as the virtualized component's ref.
isRowLoaded

Function responsible for tracking the loaded state of each row. Rows that are currently loading can be treated as loaded to avoid requesting them multiple times.
loadMoreRows

Callback to be invoked when more rows must be loaded. The returned Promise should be resolved once row data has finished loading. It will be used to determine when to refresh the list with the newly-loaded data. This callback may be called multiple times in reaction to a single scroll event.
#### Optional props
Name Description
minimumBatchSize

Minimum number of rows to be loaded at a time. This property can be used to batch requests to reduce HTTP requests.
rowCount

Number of rows in list; can be arbitrary high number if actual number is unknown.
threshold

Threshold at which to pre-fetch data. A threshold X means that data will start loading when a user scrolls within X rows.
### List It is inefficient to create and manage a large list of DOM elements within a scrolling container if only a few of those elements are visible. The primary purpose of this component is to improve performance by only rendering the DOM nodes that a user is able to see based on their current scroll position. This component renders a virtualized list of elements with either fixed or dynamic heights. #### Required props
Name Description
rowCount

Number of rows in list.
rowHeight

Either a fixed row height (number) or a function that returns the height of a row given its index: ({ index: number }): number. If function is used, specify estimatedRowSize for more consistent scrolling behavior.
rowRenderer

Responsible for rendering a row given its index. It receives index, isScrolling, isVisible, key, parent, and style parameters.

The style parameter specifies how the row is to be sized and positioned and must be passed through to the rendered row element. The key parameter must also be applied to the rendered element.
width

Width of the list.
#### Optional props
Name Description
cellRangeRenderer

Responsible for rendering a group of cells given their index ranges.

This is an advanced property. It is useful for situations where the Grid requires additional, overlayed UI (such as a Gantt chart or a calendar application). The easiest way to override it is to decorate defaultCellRangeRenderer.

Defaults to defaultCellRangeRenderer.
containerProps

Additional props (eg onWheel) to spread onto the outer Grid element.
containerStyle

Optional custom inline style to attach to inner cell-container element.
deferredMeasurementCache

If CellMeasurer is used to measure this Grid's children, this should be a pointer to its CellMeasurerCache. A shared CellMeasurerCache reference enables Grid and CellMeasurer to share measurement data.
elementRef

Reference to the outer (scrolling) DOM element.
getScrollbarSize

Returns the size of the browser's scrollbar. Exposed for testing purposes only.

Defaults to dom-helpers' scrollbarSize (which returns undefined during server rendering).
initialScrollTop

Vertical scroll offset to initially render (and scroll to) the Grid at. Only the initial value is used: changing this prop later has no effect (use scrollToPosition to scroll). This also works with server rendering: the cells at this offset are rendered on the server, and they stay in place when the page is hydrated. Ignored if a scrollElement is specified (which then determines the vertical offset).
isScrollingOptOut

Prevents re-rendering of visible cells on scroll end. (Opts out of the isScrolling param passed to cellRangeRenderer, to avoid the extra render when scroll stops.) Visible cells are still re-rendered when the Grid's props change or forceUpdate() is called.
onScrollbarPresenceChange

Called whenever a horizontal or vertical scrollbar is added or removed: ({ horizontal: boolean, size: number, vertical: boolean }): void. This prop is not intended for end-user use; it is used by MultiGrid to support fixed-row/fixed-column scroll syncing.
scrollingResetTimeInterval

Wait this amount of time (in milliseconds) after the last scroll event before resetting Grid pointer-events.
aria-label

ARIA label for the list element. There is no default label. (With role="grid", it defaults to "grid", as in version 9.)
aria-readonly

ARIA readonly attribute for the list element. Not set by default (it doesn't apply to role="list"); with role="grid", it defaults to true.
containerRole

ARIA role for the inner container of the rows. Defaults to "presentation" (so that the rows belong to the list), or to "row" with role="grid".
role

ARIA role for the list element. With the default "list", rows that don't specify a role get role="listitem" (#1657). Pass "grid" for the version 9 roles (a grid element whose rows are gridcells within a single row).
className

Optional custom CSS class name to attach to root List element.
estimatedRowSize

Used to estimate the total height of a List before all of its rows have actually been measured. The estimated total height is adjusted as rows are rendered.
height

Height constraint for list (determines how many actual rows are rendered). Required, unless a scrollElement is specified.

With a scrollElement, the height of the scroll element's viewport is used instead; this prop is then only used until the scroll element has been measured (e.g. during server rendering).
id

Optional custom id to attach to root List element.
noRowsRenderer

Callback used to render placeholder content when rowCount is 0. By default, nothing is rendered.
onRowsRendered

Callback invoked with information about the slice of rows that were just rendered: ({ overscanStartIndex: number, overscanStopIndex: number, startIndex: number, stopIndex: number }): void.
onScroll

Callback invoked whenever the scroll offset changes within the inner scrollable region: ({ clientHeight: number, scrollHeight: number, scrollTop: number }): void. This callback can be used to sync scrolling between lists, tables, or grids.
overscanIndicesGetter

Responsible for calculating the number of rows to overscan before and after a specified range. By default (accessibilityOverscanIndicesGetter), at least one row is overscanned in each direction (for accessibility). See Grid overscanIndicesGetter for details.
overscanRowCount

Number of rows to render above/below the visible bounds of the list. This can help reduce flickering during scrolling on certain browsers/devices.

Note that this property has performance implications: the higher the value, the more work needs to be done in reaction to each scroll event.
scrollElement

Element that scrolls the List (instead of the List scrolling itself): "window", or a scrollable DOM element (e.g. a container that the List is rendered within, along with other content).

The List then renders at its full height, renders only the rows visible within the scroll element's viewport, and its scroll methods scroll the scroll element. Its position within the scroll element is measured when the scroll element scrolls or is resized, and when the List re-renders (e.g. call forceUpdateGrid() if content above the List changes size without the List re-rendering). Pass null while the scroll element isn't available yet (e.g. before a ref to it has been attached); the List then renders the rows at its top.
style

Optional custom inline style to attach to root List element.
tabIndex

Optional override of tab index default.
### Masonry This component efficiently displays arbitrarily positioned cells using windowing techniques. Cell position is determined by an injected `cellPositioner` property. Windowing is vertical; this component does not support horizontal scrolling. Rendering occurs in two phases: 1) First pass uses estimated cell sizes (provided by the cache) to determine how many cells to measure in a batch. Batch size is chosen using a fast, naive layout algorithm that stacks images in order until the viewport has been filled. After measurement is complete (once the render has been committed) this component evaluates positioned cells in order to determine if another measurement pass is required (eg if actual cell sizes were less than estimated sizes). All measurements are permanently cached (keyed by `keyMapper`) for performance purposes. 2) Second pass uses the external `cellPositioner` to layout cells. At this time the positioner has access to cached size measurements for all cells. The positions it returns are cached by Masonry for fast access later. Phase one is repeated if the user scrolls beyond the current layout's bounds. If the layout is invalidated due to eg a resize, cached positions can be cleared using `recomputeCellPositions()`. Animation constraints: Simple animations are supported (eg translate/slide into place on initial reveal). More complex animations are not (eg flying from one position to another on resize). Layout constraints: This component supports multi-column layout. The height of each item may vary. The width of each item must not exceed the width of the column it is "in". The left position of all items within a column must align. (Items may not span multiple columns.) #### Required props

pkg.name: react-virtualized
pkg.description: React components for efficiently rendering large, scrollable lists and tabular data
pkg.author: Brian Vaughn <brian.david.vaughn@gmail.com> (https://github.com/bvaughn/)

scripts.e2e:install: pnpm -C integrations/tests exec playwright install --with-deps chromium

tsconfigs.tsconfig.json:
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "tsBuildInfoFile": "./node_modules/.tmp/tsconfig.app.tsbuildinfo",
    "target": "ES2022",
    "useDefineForClassFields": true,
    "lib": ["ES2022", "DOM", "DOM.Iterable"],
    "module": "ESNext",
    "skipLibCheck": true,

    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "allowImportingTsExtensions": true,
    "resolveJsonModule": true,
    "verbatimModuleSyntax": true,
    "moduleDetection": "force",
    "noEmit": true,
    "jsx": "react-jsx",

    "strict": true,
    "noUnusedLocals": true,
    "noUnusedParameters": true,
    "erasableSyntaxOnly": true,
    "noFallthroughCasesInSwitch": true,
    "noUncheckedSideEffectImports": true,

    "paths": {
      "react-virtualized": ["./lib"]
    },
    "types": [
      "csstype",
      "node",
      "vitest/globals",
      "@testing-library/jest-dom",
      "@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest"
    ]
  },
  "include": [
    "integrations",
    "lib",
    "scripts",
    "src",
    "index.tsx",
    "vitest.setup.ts"
  ]
}
